date_only.description: The source gave a day without a time.

value.description: The date as the source wrote it.

field.description: The date's path within that record.

uuid.description: Sightings and KEV entries: their UUID.

text.description: CVE 5 timeline entries: their free text, shown only (the entry has no type).

url.description: Sightings: their source, when it is an HTTP(S) URL.

metric_role.description: Optional calculation input: discovery, report, acknowledgement, disclosure, exploit_publication, exploitation, exploitation_report, patch or patch_observed.

metric_basis.description: Optional evidence basis: recorded_event, kev_first_seen, kev_report or sighting_report.

batch_listing.description: KEV exploitation inputs: dated on a day the catalog listed a batch of vulnerabilities (a backlog, not new activity).

publication_copy.description: KEV dates: the vulnerability's publication instant copied into the entry, not a listing date; shown, but not a calculation input.

added_in_revision.description: A disclosure date taken from the revision that added this vulnerability to an advisory about several, which replaces the advisory's initial release date.

linked_record.description: The date comes from a related record (a CSAF advisory, a national database entry...), not from the vulnerability's own record.

as_of.description: UTC calculation time. Future events are excluded from metrics.

anchors.description: Selected origin, discovery, report, acknowledgement, disclosure, exploit_publication, exploitation and patch events; missing anchors are null.

vendor_response_time.description: VTEM vendor response time: report to the vendor or a coordinator, to acknowledgement.

time_to_exploit.description: Earliest discovery, report or disclosure to exploitation.

disclosure_to_exploit_publication.description: Earliest disclosure/publication to the first published proof of concept.

time_to_patch.description: VTEM time to patch: report to the vendor or a coordinator, to patch evidence.

total_time_to_patch.description: VTEM total time to patch: discovery to patch evidence.

disclosure_to_patch.description: Public disclosure to patch evidence (days of risk).

time_unpatched.description: Origin to patch or as_of, clamped at zero.

exploitation_to_patch.description: Exploitation to patch or as_of; negative means patch evidence came first.

exploit_publication_to_patch.description: Published proof of concept to patch or as_of; negative means patch evidence came first.

available.description: False when a required endpoint has no dated evidence.

missing.description: Unavailable duration: missing start and/or end.

seconds.description: Nominal elapsed seconds (a bare date read as midnight UTC); signed except for time_unpatched, which is clamped at zero.

min_seconds.description: Smallest interval the endpoints' precision allows; equals seconds when both are exact.

max_seconds.description: Largest interval the endpoints' precision allows (a bare date spans its whole UTC day).

approximate.description: At least one endpoint has day precision: a bare date, or a timestamp at exactly midnight UTC.

batch_listing.description: An endpoint is a KEV batch listing: the exploitation began earlier than that date.

order_known.description: False when date-only precision does not establish which endpoint came first.

ongoing.description: No patch recorded: the endpoint is the calculation clock, not proof of an unpatched system.

end_before_start.description: The end event certainly preceded the start event; false when the order is unknown.

discovery_after_disclosure.description: total_time_to_patch: the discovery date is certainly later than public disclosure, so it most likely records when a publisher learned of the vulnerability.

end.description: Selected end evidence, or the calculation clock.

basis.description: date_published or state_published: whether a withdrawn record still counts in the period it was published in.

available.description: False when the counters have never been prepared; counts is then empty. With basis=state_published, also false unless the source's pass writes per-source counters and maintains a lifecycle index.

CnaRequestModel.title: CVE JSON record format
CnaRequestModel.description: cve-schema specifies the CVE JSON record format. This is the blueprint for a rich set of JSON data that can be submitted by CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) and Authorized Data Publishers (ADPs) to describe a CVE Record. Some examples of CVE Record data include CVE ID number, affected product(s), affected version(s), and public references. While those specific items are required when assigning a CVE, there are many other optional data in the schema that can be used to enrich CVE Records for community benefit. Learn more about the CVE program at [the official website](https://cve.mitre.org). This CVE JSON record format is defined using JSON Schema. Learn more about JSON Schema [here](https://json-schema.org/).

catalogs.description: Catalogue short name -> record count, or -> {period: count} with a granularity. These overlap: a record listed by two catalogues is counted by both, so they sum to more than `exploited` (or than `totals`).
